_about: Forge's own explainer text for each body metric (written for Forge; not copied from Withings). Shown in the metric sheet on the Body tab. noise_floor_per_week is used by trend detection (W2): smaller weekly changes are treated as noise. Units: SI, converted on screen.

weight_kg.name: Weight
weight_kg.what: Your total body weight: muscle, fat, bone, organs, water and whatever you ate and drank.
weight_kg.how: Measured directly by the scale's load cells. Very accurate for the moment you step on; the day-to-day swings are you, not the scale.
weight_kg.moves: Water and salt (often 0.5–2 kg overnight), food in your gut, carbs (stored with water), training soreness, hormones, and only slowly fat or muscle.
weight_kg.ranges: No 'good' weight on its own. Forge judges the trend against your goal: about 0.5–1% of body weight a week when cutting keeps muscle best (Helms et al., 2014).
weight_kg.caveats: Single weigh-ins are noisy. Forge smooths them into a trend and, when the scale weighs you more than once a day, uses the earliest weigh-in (morning, before food).
weight_kg.in_forge: Weigh in each morning after the bathroom, before eating. The trend sets your calorie targets.

bmi.name: BMI
bmi.what: Weight divided by height squared. A quick population screen, not a body-composition measure.
bmi.how: Calculated by Forge from your weight and height.
bmi.ranges: WHO adult categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30+ obesity.
bmi.caveats: BMI ignores muscle: a muscular lifter can read 'overweight' while lean. Look at FFMI and FMI next to it.
bmi.in_forge: Shown for reference only. Forge's goals use fat mass and the weight trend instead.

fat_ratio_pct.name: Body fat %
fat_ratio_pct.what: The share of your weight that is fat.
fat_ratio_pct.how: Estimated by bioimpedance: a tiny current through your feet, plus your height, age and sex in a formula. It estimates; it doesn't see fat.
fat_ratio_pct.moves: Real fat loss or gain over weeks, but also hydration, a recent workout, a meal, cold feet and time of day.
fat_ratio_pct.ranges: ACE categories, men: 2–5% essential, 6–13% athletes, 14–17% fitness, 18–24% average, 25%+ obese. Women: 10–13%, 14–20%, 21–24%, 25–31%, 32%+.
fat_ratio_pct.caveats: A day-to-day jump of 1–2 points is almost always water, not fat. Compare weekly or monthly averages at the same time of day.
fat_ratio_pct.in_forge: Forge watches the 28-day trend of fat mass (kg), which matters more on a cut than the percentage.

fat_mass_kg.name: Fat mass
fat_mass_kg.what: How much of your weight is fat, in kg or lb.
fat_mass_kg.how: Weight × body fat % (both from the scale).
fat_mass_kg.moves: Eating below or above maintenance over weeks. Short swings come from the fat % estimate.
fat_mass_kg.ranges: Personal: the direction over 4+ weeks is what counts.
fat_mass_kg.caveats: Inherits the noise of the fat % estimate.
fat_mass_kg.in_forge: On a cut, Forge checks this falls at a safe pace while fat-free mass holds.

fat_free_mass_kg.name: Fat-free mass
fat_free_mass_kg.what: Everything that isn't fat: muscle, bone, organs and water.
fat_free_mass_kg.moves: Muscle gain or loss, and water (glycogen, salt, hydration).
fat_free_mass_kg.ranges: FFMI (fat-free mass ÷ height²) puts it in context; natural lifters rarely exceed about 25 (Kouri et al., 1995).
fat_free_mass_kg.caveats: A drop in the first week of a diet is mostly water and glycogen.
fat_free_mass_kg.in_forge: Forge's lean-preservation check uses this during a cut (losing more than about 0.1 kg a week is a flag).

muscle_mass_kg.name: Muscle mass
muscle_mass_kg.what: The scale's estimate of muscle (including the water inside it).
muscle_mass_kg.how: Bioimpedance estimate, derived from fat-free mass.
muscle_mass_kg.moves: Training and protein over months; hydration day to day.
muscle_mass_kg.ranges: Personal: compare with yourself over 8+ weeks.
muscle_mass_kg.caveats: Changes of a few hundred grams are within the estimate's error. Muscle grows slowly (well under 0.5 kg a month for most people).
muscle_mass_kg.in_forge: Shown next to your weekly training sets, so you can see whether volume and muscle move together.

hydration_kg.name: Water
hydration_kg.moves: Drinking, sweating, salt, carbs, alcohol, illness.
hydration_kg.ranges: Roughly half to two-thirds of body weight in adults; leaner people sit higher.
hydration_kg.caveats: This is the number that explains most surprise weight jumps.
hydration_kg.in_forge: When weight jumps and water jumps with it, Forge calls it water, not fat (W2 trend cards).

bone_mass_kg.name: Bone mass
bone_mass_kg.what: The scale's estimate of the mineral weight of your skeleton.
bone_mass_kg.how: Estimated from fat-free mass with a formula; not a bone-density scan.
bone_mass_kg.ranges: Typically a few percent of body weight.
bone_mass_kg.caveats: Not a substitute for a DEXA bone-density test. Ignore week-to-week changes.

heart_pulse_bpm.name: Standing heart rate
heart_pulse_bpm.what: Your heart rate while standing on the scale.
heart_pulse_bpm.how: Measured through the feet while you stand still.
heart_pulse_bpm.moves: Time since waking, coffee, stress, poor sleep, illness, fitness over months.
heart_pulse_bpm.ranges: 60–100 bpm is the usual adult resting range (American Heart Association); standing reads a bit higher than lying down.
heart_pulse_bpm.caveats: Not the same as resting heart rate from your Watch overnight. Compare like with like.
heart_pulse_bpm.in_forge: From W2, shown next to your Watch's overnight resting heart rate.

visceral_fat.name: Visceral fat
visceral_fat.what: An index for fat stored around the organs in your abdomen.
visceral_fat.how: Withings' own bioimpedance estimate, given as an index rather than kg.
visceral_fat.moves: Overall fat loss or gain; it usually falls early in a fat-loss phase.
visceral_fat.ranges: Withings' index has no published external standard. Compare with yourself over months.
visceral_fat.caveats: An estimate, not an MRI. Only returned if your Withings API plan includes it (see the data check).

bmr_kcal.name: BMR
bmr_kcal.what: Basal metabolic rate: the calories your body burns at complete rest.
bmr_kcal.how: From the scale if Withings returns it; otherwise Forge estimates it (Mifflin–St Jeor, 1990).
bmr_kcal.caveats: Any BMR from a scale or formula is an estimate, often 5–10% off.
bmr_kcal.in_forge: A floor for your calorie targets; adaptive TDEE (Checkpoint C) learns your real burn from your logs.

metabolic_age.name: Metabolic age
metabolic_age.what: The age whose average BMR matches yours.
metabolic_age.how: Withings compares your BMR with age-group averages.
metabolic_age.moves: Mostly muscle mass and body size.
metabolic_age.ranges: Lower than your real age is the usual hope; it's a comparison, not a health measure.
metabolic_age.caveats: An estimate built on another estimate. Not medical.
metabolic_age.in_forge: Shown if returned; labelled as an estimate.

vascular_age.name: Vascular age
vascular_age.what: An estimate of how stiff your arteries are, as an age.
vascular_age.how: From pulse wave velocity measured by the scale through your feet.
vascular_age.caveats: Probably not on the free API. Still free to view in the Withings app. Not a diagnosis.
vascular_age.in_forge: Shown if returned; otherwise a monthly manual entry.

vo2max.name: VO₂max
vo2max.what: An estimate of the most oxygen your body can use per minute per kilogram: a summary of cardio fitness.
vo2max.how: Withings estimates it from your heart rate and activity (watch) or from a scale's cardio measurements, not from a lab test.
vo2max.moves: Regular cardio, especially harder intervals, raises it over weeks; losing fat raises it too, because it's per kilogram.
vo2max.ranges: Depends a lot on age and sex; roughly 35–45 is average for adult men, higher is fitter.
vo2max.caveats: An estimate. Watch the trend rather than single readings.

nerve_health_score.name: Nerve Health Score
nerve_health_score.what: A score for the small nerves in your feet that control sweating.
nerve_health_score.how: A guided measurement on the scale (electrochemical skin conductance).
nerve_health_score.moves: Changes slowly; your doctor can interpret it.
nerve_health_score.caveats: Probably not on the free API. Not a diagnosis.
nerve_health_score.in_forge: Shown if returned; otherwise a manual entry.

ffmi.name: FFMI
ffmi.what: Fat-free mass index: fat-free mass divided by height squared. BMI for lean mass.
ffmi.ranges: Around 18–20 is typical for untrained men, 15–17 for women; natural lifters rarely pass about 25 (Kouri et al., 1995).
ffmi.in_forge: Shown next to BMI so a muscular build isn't mislabelled.

fmi.name: FMI
fmi.what: Fat mass index: fat mass divided by height squared.
fmi.ranges: Reference bands by sex in Kyle et al., 2003 (used by the Forge Score from W2).
